implemented: Retired adapters cannot delete or reset. Queued deletions that time out before starting do not run.
Explicit account reset retires same-bridge/key bindings, blocks stale operations, aborts requests, serializes behind in-flight storage work, and removes session, PKCE and user slots.
Failure or deadline leaves the lane quarantined; a fresh port on the same bridge can retry.

timeoutInvestigation.method: metadata-only; no contents restored, flags altered or packages installed
timeoutInvestigation.previousMetroAndNativeTypeTimeouts: prior security handoff records bounded timeouts; no retry while native dependencies are offloaded
timeoutInvestigation.cause: offloading is a plausible blocker, but no exact hanging file was established

limitations: Explicit reset must occur before closing old binding or starting new account; it clears local storage but is not server signout or revocation.
Generation and quarantine are in-memory and scoped to the same bridge object and storage key; separate bridge proxies, processes, crashes and restarts require native durable coordination.
Concurrent active adapters without an account-handover barrier remain a caller ownership responsibility.
An already-sent network request or already-started native write may complete.
Actual native bridge, production identity, storage, authorization and device testing remain unverified.
